spec: Given a time string 'HH:MM' in 24-hour format and a non-negative integer number of minutes to subtract, return the resulting time as an 'HH:MM' string, wrapping around backward past midnight if necessary (day boundaries are not tracked).

Given a non-negative integer total number of minutes (which may span multiple days), format it as a string 'Dd HH:MM' where D is the number of whole days elapsed, and HH:MM is the time of day remaining, both zero-padded appropriately (D is not zero-padded).
Given a year and a quarter number (1-4), return the (year, month, day) of the first day of that calendar quarter.
Convert an integer number of seconds, known to satisfy 0 <= seconds < 3600, into a string "M:SS": the minutes part has no leading zero, the seconds part is always exactly two digits.

Convert a non-negative integer number of seconds into a string "Dd HH:MM:SS" giving whole days, then hours, minutes and seconds zero-padded to two digits each. The day count has no leading zeros and may be zero.
Parse a string of the form "Dd HH:MM:SS" (a non-negative integer day count, then hours, minutes and seconds each two digits) and return the total number of whole seconds it represents.

Convert a (possibly negative) integer number of seconds into a signed clock string: the absolute value is formatted as "HH:MM:SS" (each field zero-padded to two digits, hours may exceed two digits), preceded by a "-" if the input was negative, or by nothing if it was zero or positive.

Parse a signed clock string, optionally beginning with "-", followed by "HH:MM:SS" (each field a non-negative integer, hours may have more than two digits), and return the total number of seconds it represents as a signed integer.

Convert a non-negative integer number of milliseconds, known to be less than 3600000 (under one hour), into a stopwatch string "MM:SS.mmm": minutes and seconds zero-padded to two digits, milliseconds zero-padded to three digits.
Parse a stopwatch string "MM:SS.mmm" (minutes, seconds and milliseconds each a fixed-width non-negative integer) into the total number of whole milliseconds it represents.
Given a birth date and a current date, each as a (year, month, day) tuple with the current date on or after the birth date, return the person's age in whole completed years.

Given a birth date and a current date, each as a (year, month, day) tuple with the current date on or after the birth date, return the elapsed age as a (years, months) tuple of whole completed years and additional whole completed months (0-11).

Given a birthday as a (month, day) tuple and today's date as a (year, month, day) tuple, return the number of days from today until the next occurrence of that birthday, where 0 means the birthday is today. The birthday's day-of-month is never 29 in February.

Given a birthday as a (month, day) tuple and today's date as a (year, month, day) tuple, return the calendar year in which the person's next birthday (including today, if today is the birthday) falls.

Given two dates d1 and d2, each a (year, month, day) tuple with d2 on or after d1, return the number of whole months elapsed from d1 to d2: the difference in (year*12 + month), reduced by one if d2's day-of-month is earlier than d1's.

Given two birth dates birth1 and birth2, each a (year, month, day) tuple, return the string "first" if birth1 represents an earlier (older) birth date than birth2, "second" if birth2 is earlier, or "same" if they are equal.

Given a birth date as a (year, month, day) tuple, a target whole-number age, and today's date as a (year, month, day) tuple, return how many more whole years (an integer, possibly zero or negative) until the person reaches the target age, computed as target_age minus the person's current whole-years age on today's date.

Given two birth dates birth1 and birth2, each a (year, month, day) tuple, and today's date as a (year, month, day) tuple, return the signed difference in whole-years age between the first and second person on today's date (age1 minus age2). Both people were already born on today's date.

Given a year, a month (1-12), a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) and n (1-5), return the day-of-month (an integer) of the n-th occurrence of that weekday in that month. It is guaranteed that the n-th occurrence exists.
Given a year, a month (1-12) and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return how many times that weekday occurs in that month (either 4 or 5).

Given a year, a month (1-12), a starting day-of-month, and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return the day-of-month (an integer) of the first occurrence of that weekday on or after the given day, guaranteed to still fall in the same month.

Given a year, a month (1-12), a starting day-of-month, and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return the day-of-month (an integer) of the last occurrence of that weekday on or before the given day, guaranteed to still fall in the same month.

Given a year, a month (1-12), a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) and n (1-5), return the day-of-month (an integer) of the n-th-from-last occurrence of that weekday in that month, where n=1 means the last occurrence. It is guaranteed that the n-th-from-last occurrence exists.

Given a year, a month (1-12) and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return a (first_day, last_day) tuple of day-of-month integers giving the first and last occurrences of that weekday in the month.
Given a year and a month (1-12), return a (saturday_count, sunday_count) tuple giving the number of Saturdays and the number of Sundays in that month.
Convert a date string of the form "D/M/YYYY" (day and month each one or two digits, year exactly four digits) into the zero-padded ISO form "YYYY-MM-DD".
Convert a date string of the form "YYYY-M-D" (year exactly four digits, month and day each one or two digits) into the zero-padded ISO form "YYYY-MM-DD".

Return True if the given string is a valid combined date and time in strict "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" format (a valid ISO date, a single space, then a valid HH:MM:SS time with hours 0-23), and False otherwise.
Convert a zero-padded ISO date string "YYYY-MM-DD" into the compact form "YYYY-M-D" with any leading zero removed from the month and day (but the year keeps all four digits).
Convert a zero-padded date string "DD-MM-YYYY" into the ISO form "YYYY-MM-DD", keeping all digits and separators the same, just reordering the fields.
Convert a zero-padded ISO date string "YYYY-MM-DD" into the form "DD-MM-YYYY", keeping all digits and separators the same, just reordering the fields.
Convert a date string "YY-MM-DD" with a two-digit year into full "YYYY-MM-DD" form: years 00-69 become 20YY, and years 70-99 become 19YY. Month and day are left unchanged.
Given a list of strings, return how many of them are valid dates in strict "YYYY-MM-DD" format (four-digit year, real month 1-12, day valid for that month and year including leap years).

Given a time of day as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and an integer offset in hours (which may be negative or span more than a day), return a (new_hour, new_minute, day_delta) tuple: the resulting time-of-day and the signed number of days the date moves by.

Given a time of day as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and an integer offset in minutes (which may be negative or span more than a day), return a (new_hour, new_minute, day_delta) tuple: the resulting time-of-day and the signed number of days the date moves by.

Given a local time string "HH:MM", the UTC offset (in minutes) of the zone it is currently expressed in, and the UTC offset (in minutes) of a target zone, return a (new_time_str, day_delta) tuple: the equivalent time in the target zone as "HH:MM" and the signed number of days the date shifts by.

Given a UTC time as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and a UTC offset in minutes for a local zone (which may be negative), return a (local_hour, local_minute, day_delta) tuple: the local time-of-day and the signed number of days the date shifts by relative to the UTC date.

Given a departure time string "HH:MM", a non-negative flight duration in minutes, and the difference in minutes between the destination's and origin's UTC offsets, return a (arrival_time_str, day_delta) tuple: the local arrival time as "HH:MM" and how many days later (or earlier) the arrival calendar date is.

Given an hour and a minute that may be out of the usual 0-23 / 0-59 ranges (either negative or too large), return a (norm_hour, norm_minute, day_delta) tuple representing the same point in time with hour in 0-23, minute in 0-59, and day_delta the signed number of days this normalization crosses.

Given a time of day as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and two integer minute offsets to apply in sequence, return a (new_hour, new_minute, day_delta) tuple giving the resulting time-of-day after applying both offsets together and the signed number of days the date moves by.
